newsitem.title: USA: U.S. troops will stay in Bosnia until March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops will stay in Bosnia until March.

text.p: About 5,000 U.S. troops will begin moving into Bosnia from Germany in the next few days to cover the withdrawal of international peacekeeping troops this year, and that protective force will remain in Bosnia until March, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

"It (the cover force) is scheduled to depart in March," Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters. That would be more than two months after the mission of the current NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) ends on Dec. 20.

Asked when the previously-planned cover force would move into Bosnia, Bacon said: "I would expect in the next couple of days." He said he expected a preliminary order for movement of the force to be signed this week.

Bacon stressed that NATO and the United States had made no decision yet on whether a follow-on force to IFOR would be sent to Bosnia next year, saying that the cover force was only to provide security for removal of the 52,000 IFOR troops. The peacekeeers include 15,800 U.S. soldiers.
Most of the current IFOR troops will remain in Bosnia until local elections are held there in November and then begin a rapid drawdown, expected to end in January.
"The coming (cover) force will remain after IFOR goes" until March, Bacon said. "It will go in and perform security functions after IFOR packs up and goes."
